I bought the a Vive kit for $800 about 2 years ago,

Space: I set it up in a 10x11 foot room with about 10x7 space to play. It's not nearly enough room to really let yourself get into the games. Ideally, you would probably want a 25x25 or even a 50x50 foot playspace. Because of the space limitation, you end up either punching walls or standing mostly still and using the controllers to move yourself around in a game. Every time you run into a wall it takes you completely out of the experience. At 50x50 feet you could explore a haunted house or pretty much anything if they could figure out how to redirect you so that even though you are walking in circles, it feels like you are moving forward, but you would need a lot of space for something like that to feel natural.

Sensors: In order to move around in the virtual environment, you need censors in the corners. The original Vive came with 2 sensors, but it really needs one in each corner for accuracy, which I hear the new version allows for.

Movement: Nothing takes you out of the game more than constantly worrying about the wire you drag with you everywhere. The wire isn't the only problem though, trying to move around quickly or do odd movements with a massive headset on your head isn't easy. It falls to far forward or backwards to easily. Wireless is the only way to go, but even then, until they figure out how not to have 10 pounds strapped to your head, it will never be as fun as it could be.

Graphics: What people who haven't seen VR yet probably don't know is that you have to stare at the center of the goggles all the time. You can't move your eyes left to right or up to down, you have to move your head. Everything gets blurry off center. The goggles put you inside this amazing world, but it's as though you can only enjoy it looking through bottle cap sized glasses. Everything is also pretty blurry, even at center. I hear the new Vive addresses this with a higher resolution, but I haven't used one of the new headsets yet to see how much better it is.

Software: It's not bad, but still glitchy. Every time I don't use it for awhile, I have to spend 10-30 minutes getting updated and working again. The cubes use bluetooth, which is hit or miss. Connections seem solid once connected, but getting connected is sketchy. Using the software in game is also painful. Sure, you can have a 50 foot screen in game, but you can only see a bottle cap portion of it at a time. I'm a computer guy through and through, but I wish they would make a device dedicated to VR, like a VR gaming system. I know Playstation sort of has this, but it really needs to be a machine dedicated to one thing, VR.

Dizziness: This is probably the biggest issue that isn't mentioned much. If you try playing for an hour straight, you will be dizzy and most likely feel sick for hours afterwards. Some people can only play for 10 minutes and I've seen some who can go over an hour, but almost everybody starts to feel ill at one point or another. It makes it hard to get excited about playing knowing that you will feel sick afterwards.

Games: Some of the games are incredible. Most of the games are terrible. Most of the games become boring really quickly. I wouldn't play most of the games if they weren't in 3D.

Overall: Despite all its downfalls, it's one of the most amazing experiences you'll ever have. I'm personally going to wait a few more years until they get higher resolution, wireless, lighter headsets, and figure out how to combat the dizziness.
